$comment: Refusals the playback compiler raises against constructs a user can author. An entry records who owns the refusal and why it stands; it is not a claim that the refusal is correct. status=live-defect means the document is authorable today and unplayable, and the refusal is a placeholder for work that has not happened; status=intended means the refusal is the answer. Enforced by tools/scripts/negative_capability_check.py.

refusals.reason: A nested MIDI leaf with authored groove refuses when SequenceRef trimming changes its source window, because groove displacement can move events across either retained boundary and the compiler has no defined chase, clip or discard rule; the refusal stands until source-window groove inheritance is specified.

A nested RegisteredContent leaf refuses when SequenceRef trimming changes its source window, because the trusted compile input carries only the flattened duration and owner context position, not the authored source offset and original duration needed to preserve pattern phase; the refusal stands until source-window provenance is part of the renderer contract.

set_clip_sequence_ref composes with set_clip_playback_properties, set_track_mixer, set_track_freeze and the take, automation and device-chain surfaces, but flattening has nowhere to fold clip gain and fades, a child fader, a child device chain, takes, freeze, a non-musical anchor, or a trim that cuts a conformed source or a fade, so each of those authored combinations refuses instead of playing wrong.
